claim: Driving distance from Saint-Méloir-des-Ondes to Mont-Saint-Michel is roughly 45 km, about 47 minutes via N176 and D4.
quote: The driving distance from Saint-Méloir-des-Ondes to Mont-Saint-Michel is approximately 45 kilometers, taking about 47 minutes. The route is primarily via N 176 and D 4.

claim: Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey 2026 entry is €16 from 1 April–30 September and €13 from 1 October–31 March; free for under-18s and EU residents aged 18–25.
quote: April 1 – September 30: Individual ticket: €16 ... October 1 – March 31: Individual ticket: €13 ... Free Admission: Children under 18 (families only); Ages 18-25 from EU countries

claim: Abbey opens 9:00–19:00 from 1 May to 31 August and 9:30–18:00 the rest of the year; last entry one hour before closing; exceptional closure Monday 1 June 2026.
quote: May 1 – August 31: 9am - 7pm; September 1 – April 30: 9:30am - 6pm. Last entry occurs one hour before closing ... exceptional closure on Monday, June 1, 2026.

claim: La Caserne parking (mid-season Mar–Jun) costs €16 for 3h, €19 for 6h, €22 for 24h in 2026; first 30 minutes free.
quote: Mid Season (Mar 1-Jun 30 & Sep 1-Nov 1): Light vehicle up to 3h: €16; Light vehicle up to 6h: €19; Light vehicle 24h: €22. Free first 30 minutes year-round.

claim: Le Passeur free shuttle runs 7:30–23:00 in mid-season with a maximum wait of about 12 minutes, dropping passengers 350 m from the ramparts.
quote: Mid/High seasons (Mar-Oct): 7:30am–11pm ... Maximum wait of 12 minutes ... The shuttle terminus is 350 m from the ramparts of Mont-Saint-Michel

claim: La Caserne parking sits in Beauvoir 2.5 km from the abbey with ~4,000 spaces; the walking alternative along the pedestrian causeway takes 35–45 minutes.
quote: Located in Beauvoir ... approximately 4,000 spaces situated 2.5 kilometers from the abbey ... Distance: 2.5 kilometers via pedestrian walkway; Time Required: 35 to 45 minutes to reach the main abbey entrance

claim: April 18, 2026 is the highest spring tide of the year at the Mont with coefficient 105 (high tide 08:35), with neighbouring days April 17 (101), 19 (104), 20 (99).
quote: April 18 (highest of the year): Coefficient 105, high tide at 08:35; April 17: Coefficient 101, high tide at 07:55; April 19: Coefficient 104, high tide at 09:15; April 20: Coefficient 99, high tide at 09:55

claim: May 16–19, 2026 shows elevated coefficients (96–99) qualifying as spring tides but not reaching the coefficient-100 island-cutoff threshold.
quote: May 16: Coefficient 96, high tide at 07:22; May 17: Coefficient 99, high tide at 08:09; May 18: Coefficient 99, high tide at 08:56; May 19: Coefficient 95, high tide at 09:43. None of the May dates reach the coefficient-100 threshold

claim: June 2026 peaks at coefficient 95 on the 16th (with 93 on the 15th and 94 on the 17th) — borderline spring tide, well below the island-flooding 110 threshold.
quote: June 16, 2026: Coefficient 95 (the month's highest) ... June 15 (coefficient 93) and June 17 (coefficient 94)

claim: A coefficient of about 110 is required for the sea to fully surround the Mount and flood the causeway, turning it back into an island.
quote: At a coefficient of 110, the Mont-Saint-Michel becomes an island again.
